texts.preamble: Ketan Thakur (Dar) vs Shubham Sharma (28/18 Badarpur) on 2 April, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No: 405/18 Ketan Thakur vs. Shubham Sharma Cnr No: Dlse01-002267-2018 1. Ketan Thakur S/o Sh. Pramod Kumar R/o House no. 64/D1, Railway colony, Thughlakabad, Jaitpur, South Delhi New Delhi-110044. ......Petitioner Versus 1. Shubham Sharma S/o Sh. Narender Kumar Sharma R/o House no.1502, Gali no.2, new Baslwa colony, Faridabad, Haryana . .......Driver cum owner/Respondent no.1 2. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Office at: Connaught Place New Delhi ......Insurance Company/Respondent no.2 Mact No.405/18 Ketan Thakur vs. Shubham Sharma & anr. P.No. 1 of 20 ss Digitally signed by Charu Charu Gupta Gupta Date: 2025.04.02 16:44:41 +0530 Date of accident : 21.01.2018 Result of accident : Injury/permanent disability Date of filing of Dar : 19.03.2018 Date of Decision : 02.04.2025 Award 1. The present DAR (detailed accident report) arises out of an accident that occurred on 21.01.2018, resulting in grievous injury to the victim/claimant Ketan Thakur.
texts.facts: 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 21.01.2018 petitioner was going for tuition towards Badarpur Market. 3. An FIR no. 0028/2018, dated 21.01.2018 was registered u/s 279/337 of IPC against respondent no.1 (driver of the offending vehicle). The offending bike was seized on the same day from the spot and driver of the offending vehicle was arrested. Upon investigation a chargesheet u/s 279/338 of IPC was filed before concerned criminal court and a DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver cum owner and respondent no.2 is the insurance company with which such offending vehicle was insured. He further pleaded that he was having a valid driving licence and his vehicle was duly insured. The insurance company filed a legal offer which was declined by the petitioner. 6. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 31.10.2018. Thereafter, evidence was led by the petitioner by examining himself as PW-1. PW-1/petitioner Ketan Thakur tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A wherein he reiterated the contents of the DAR and relied upon documents i.e. Adhar Card as Ex.PW1/1, Passport as Ex.PW1/2, Educational proof as Ex.PW1/3, MLC as Ex.PW1/4, discharge summary and OPD Card as Ex.PW1/5 (colly), Medical bills as Ex. PW1/6, photographs of injury as Ex.PW1/7, DAR as Ex.PW1/8(colly) and School I-Card marked as Mark-A. PW-1 was not cross examined by respondent no.1 and 2 despite opportunity. the injured Ketan Thakur suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 21.01.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing no. HR-51BK-6245 (Motorcycle) driven and owned by R1 and insured with R2? OPP. 10. In the present case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1 to prove the factum as well as manner of the accident. He categorically deposed that the accident occurred at the time when he was crossing Mathura Road. In his cross examination by Ld.counsel for respondent no.1, PW-1 admitted that there was no red light at the crossing nor was there any zebra crossing at the spot. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner/ claimant and against the respondents.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. It is in this view that respondents have taken a defence that it was the petitioner who was negligent in crossing the road without a red light or a zebra crossing and hence should be MACT No.405/18 Ketan Thakur vs. Shubham Sharma & anr. P.No. 4 of 20 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.04.02 16:44:52 +0530 disentitled to the claim or atleast deduction qua contributory negligence be made. This Tribunal has carefully perused the site plan annexed with the DAR which has been relied upon by the petitioner and not denied by the respondents. Such site plan cleary shows that the accident occurred not at the crossing or any junction where there could have been diverging traffic but in the middle of the road. Petitioner could have been said to be negligent had the accident occurred at a junction of a crossing however where the accident occures in the middle of the road, it is primarily the responsibility of the person driving a vehicle to be careful enough to foresee any object or person entering the middle of the road. Certainly, the offending motorbike must have been at a high speed which made it impossible for it to apply brakes timely or avert the accident. Further, merely because the entire road did not have a red light but did have sufficient space for vehicles to turn and particularly did not have any demarcated crossing for the padestrian or a footover bridge, negligence of the petitioner cannot be assumed. 11. Further, even the police, after investigation had filed chargesheet against respondent no.1 under Section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent no.1 in causing the accident. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that Ketan Thakur (Dar) vs Shubham Sharma (28/18 Badarpur) on 2 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150400229/ 3 completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 12. The driver of the offending vehicle has not entered the witness box or raised any defence to negate or refute the MACT No.405/18 Ketan Thakur vs. Shubham Sharma & anr. P.No. 5 of 20 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.04.02 16:44:55 +0530 allegations of rash and negligent driving. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 15. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & ors. v. Delhi Transport corporation & ors. ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.04.02 16:44:59 +0530 (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. This means that he is to be compensated for Ketan Thakur (Dar) vs Shubham Sharma (28/18 Badarpur) on 2 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150400229/ 4 16. Further it is noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). Hon'ble SC and Hon'ble High Courts contain necessary guidelines for award under these heads, if necessary. 16.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: "10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps. On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be MACT No.405/18 Ketan Thakur vs. Shubham Sharma & anr. P.No. 9 of 20 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.04.02 16:45:11 +0530 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less. Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity, taking note of the reduced earning Ketan Thakur (Dar) vs Shubham Sharma (28/18 Badarpur) on 2 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150400229/ 6 capacity. 27. Thus, sufficient discretion has been given to the Tribunal not to insist on investment of the compensation amount in long term fixed deposit and to release even the whole amount in the case of literate persons.
